title: EU Migration Pact Enters Full Application — Five-Year Reform Reshapes Asylum and Border Rules
detail: The New Pact on Migration and Asylum entered full legal application across the EU on June 12, 2026, exactly two years after its 2024 entry into force. The ten-law package introduces mandatory screening and security checks at external borders, faster asylum procedures for border cases, a solidarity mechanism letting member states choose between relocating asylum seekers, paying financial contributions, or providing operational support, and expanded biometric data-sharing through Eurodac. Home Affairs Commissioner Magnus Brunner called it a 'historic moment,' though the Commission's final progress report had flagged that only 14 of 27 member states submitted national implementation plans by the December deadline. Italy, Hungary, and Austria signalled they would test the limits of the new solidarity mechanism, while rights groups warned the expanded border procedures risk normalising detention, including of children.

title: Commission Proposes €540M Farm Relief Package as Middle East Crisis Drives Up Fertiliser Costs
detail: The European Commission proposed on June 12, 2026 to mobilise €540 million to help farmers cope with soaring fertiliser costs — a knock-on effect of the Middle East crisis, since natural gas is both fuel and feedstock for nitrogen fertiliser production. The package let member states redirect Common Agricultural Policy funds more flexibly, advance direct payments earlier in 2026, and top up national support by up to 200% — bringing total potential support to €1.5 billion — alongside a proposed €300 million boost to the EU's agricultural reserve.
